A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAPD research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-MRF experiments, LLaDA and Dream benchmark evaluations, and decoding-behavior analysis using aggregated TriviaQA questions.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds decoding-variant results, throughput measurements, and generation-length, block-count, and attention-layer analyses.

M1.justification: v2 introduces optional DAPD-Direct, which commits confidence-1.0 tokens before dependency-aware selection at every step (Remark 4.1; Appendix A). The attention-graph and greedy independent-set framework remains. The default is named DAPD-Staged and clarified as retaining dependency selection while enabling a late confidence shortcut.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic MRF data, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, Math500, IFEval, ParallelBench subtasks, and aggregated TriviaQA questions. Longer generation budgets and different block counts change settings within retained tasks, rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Original confidence-based token-by-token decoding to the HumanEval throughput comparison (Table 6); v1 evaluated it in the TriviaQA analysis. Fast-dLLM, EB-Sampler, and KLASS remain the principal comparators. Newly discussed DAWN and Li et al. are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds tokens-per-second evaluation, generation budgets of 512 and 1024, DAPD block-count comparisons, and controlled attention-layer selections. Reported ParallelBench settings also change: DAPD's threshold schedule changes from [0.001, 0.005] to [0.01, 0.2] for Staged, and KLASS's KL threshold changes from 0.001 to 0.01. These are substantial protocol additions and revisions, without establishing which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 tests direct confidence commits versus staged decoding, efficiency at longer generation lengths, the accuracy-throughput consequences of block-wise decoding, and dependency recovery using different attention layers (Tables 3–4, 7–8, and 10). These substantially extend the existing threshold-distribution and decoding-trajectory analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions describe 30 independently trained synthetic models and 100 random sampling paths, retaining the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 9. The added experiments do not introduce new seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for DAPD-Direct, throughput, generation length, block count, and layer selection. For example, Table 6 newly reports DAPD HumanEval throughput of 106.0 TPS, and Table 10 reports AUC 0.93 using the last two layers versus 0.73 using the first layer. Figure 4 changes alongside revised ParallelBench settings, so its differences are not same-setting gains. Figure 3 and Table 2 retain their earlier results.

T1.justification: Remark 4.1 adds the mathematical argument that a probability-one marginal fixes that token in every compatible joint distribution, supporting direct commits. The existing MRF definition, degree proxy, OVR definition, and graph-coloring relaxation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: training-free attention-based dependency selection improves accuracy–steps trade-offs and enables globally dispersed decoding. The expanded conclusion reiterates the existing graph-coloring perspective rather than redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explicitly qualifies the MRF as a heuristic conflict graph rather than exact probabilistic inference and acknowledges dependence on threshold schedules and attention-layer choices. Appendix A adds interpretations of Direct's latency trade-off, length scaling, and the loss of global parallelism under blocking.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies averaging all attention heads over the final 30% of layers in the main models, documents DAPD-Direct's task-specific threshold schedules, and supplies a project-access link. These improve disclosure; the layer specification alone does not establish that the earlier implementation changed. Existing hardware and toy-training details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds Li et al. (2026) and Luo et al.'s DAWN, distinguishing DAPD from probabilistic output augmentation and attention-based confidence relaxation. This is a focused extension of research positioning. Most other bibliography changes update publication metadata for existing references.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title and author-credit text, expands the conclusion, and edits explanatory passages. It exchanges the main-experiment and toy-experiment appendices, folds qualitative examples into Appendix C, and adds a discussion appendix. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tabular presentation with benchmark and variant tables, throughput and sensitivity tables, and a layer-ablation table. It expands the baseline-settings table to include previously plotted EOS-suppressed results, reformats retained tables, and redraws and relocates Figure 4. Figure 3 and the qualitative examples are retained rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical validation with throughput measurements, including a common four-block comparison in Table 8, and adds useful design analyses, implementation details, and explicit heuristic limitations. However, numerical reporting remains inconsistent: EB-Sampler HumanEval steps are 110.4 in Table 3 versus 112.1 in Table 5, while default DAPD-Staged GSM8K accuracy is 71.7 in Table 3 versus 70.7 in Table 7 without an explained setting difference. The additions improve support and transparency, but these discrepancies temper the overall gain.
